data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The safest protocol treats the workspace as a Merkle-DAG of pending side effects with content-addressed evidence nodes; it must durably record the root hash of the problem-specific DAG and the set of merged evidence nodes.","counterconditions":[{"case":"The DAG storage layer permits node mutation rather than strict append-only behavior.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"Garbage collection is not reachability-safe and may prune evidence nodes that lack active references.","eval":"observation"},{"case":"The merge function for unmaterialized effects is non-deterministic across reclamation attempts.","eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Instead of a mutable workspace, all pending mutations are unmerged leaves in a Merkle-DAG. Completed evidence is a node in this DAG with a stable cryptographic address. Reclamation never overwrites; it simply garbage-collects orphaned unmerged leaves that are not ancestors of any evidence node. Because evidence is content-addressed, there is no file path or mutable slot to displace. The protocol durably records the root hash of the problem-specific DAG and the set of merged evidence nodes at the time of any commit, ensuring that reclamation is structurally a prune operation on orphaned leaves only.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
